title: Influence of dexamethasone on the interaction between glucocorticoid receptor and SOX9: A molecular dynamics study.
authors: Stojceski, Filip; Buetti-Dinh, Antoine; Stoddart, Martin J; Danani, Andrea; Della Bella, Elena; Grasso, Gianvito
one_liner_zh: 该文通过分子动力学模拟研究地塞米松对糖皮质激素受体GR与转录因子SOX9相互作用的影响，聚焦于转录因子-转录因子界面动态结合机制，虽非TF-DNA体系，但方法可迁移至TF-DNA互作研究。
abstract: The glucocorticoid receptor (GR) is a nuclear receptor that controls critical biological processes by regulating the transcription of specific genes. GR transcriptional activity is modulated by a series of ligands and coenzymes, where a ligand can act as an agonist or antagonist. GR agonists, such as the glucocorticoids dexamethasone (DEX) and prednisolone, are widely prescribed to patients with inflammatory and autoimmune diseases. DEX is also used to induce osteogenic differentiation in vitro. Recently, it has been highlighted that DEX induces changes in the osteogenic differentiation of human mesenchymal stromal cells by downregulating the transcription factor SRY-box transcription factor 9 (SOX9) and upregulating the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARG). SOX9 is fundamental in the control of chondrogenesis, but also in osteogenesis by acting as a dominant-negative of RUNX2. Many processes remain to be clarified during cell fate determination, such as the interplay between the key transcription factors. The main objective pursued by this work is to shed light on the interaction between GR and SOX9 in the presence and absence of DEX at an atomic level of resolution using molecular dynamics simulations. The outcome of this research could help the understanding of possible molecular interactions between GR and SOX9 and their role in the determination of cell fate. The results highlight the key residues at the interface between GR and SOX9 involved in the complexation process and shed light on the mechanism through which DEX modulates GR-SOX9 binding and exerts its biological activity.
abstract_zh: 糖皮质激素受体（GR）是一种核受体，通过调控特定基因的转录来控制关键生物过程。GR的转录活性受一系列配体和辅酶调节，其中配体可作为激动剂或拮抗剂发挥作用。GR激动剂，如糖皮质激素地塞米松（DEX）和泼尼松龙，被广泛用于炎症和自身免疫性疾病患者的处方治疗。DEX也用于体外诱导成骨分化。近期研究表明，DEX通过下调转录因子SRY-box转录因子9（SOX9）和上调过氧化物酶体增殖物激活受体γ（PPARG）来改变人间充质基质细胞的成骨分化。SOX9在控制软骨形成中至关重要，同时通过作为RUNX2的显性负性调节因子参与成骨过程。在细胞命运决定过程中，许多机制仍有待阐明，例如关键转录因子之间的相互作用。本研究的主要目标是通过分子动力学模拟，在原子分辨率水平上阐明DEX存在和不存在情况下GR与SOX9之间的相互作用。该研究结果有助于理解GR与SOX9之间可能的分子相互作用及其在细胞命运决定中的作用。结果突出了GR与SOX9界面上参与复合物形成过程的关键残基，并揭示了DEX调节GR-SOX9结合及发挥其生物活性的机制。
